question: Do direct 17-joint and contour64 autoregressive outputs work for full-image multi-person human multi-task VLM fine-tuning?
verdict: Not as previously designed. Direct pose coordinates have credible box-conditioned evidence; direct polygons have only moderate AP. No matched work supports concatenating all people, poses, masks, and attributes into one long Qwen response at high precision.

evidence.finding: Box-conditioned polygon and keypoint sequence generation; multi-task 1024 COCO mask AP 38.2 and keypoint AP 64.8.
Direct keypoint text reaches 77.4 AP with GT boxes; not full-scene owner discovery.
Human-centric VLM directly emits pose coordinates, but pose is manually scored on 120 images and no segmentation task is included.
Explicitly calls polygons suboptimal; 16 mask-token embedding retrieval yields 45.8 COCO mask AP on InternVL2.5-8B and parallelizes multi-prediction tasks.
Uses routing/super-link queries with GroundingDINO mask and UniPose decoders; 47.8 mask AP and 74.0 pose AP.
High-fidelity human multi-task perception uses one Human Query plus task heads and owner-aware matching; 65.8 mask AP and 69.3 pose AP in the paper protocol.
Basic polygon mode is not evaluated; authors recommend grounding then crop and dense segmentation because point precision is limited.

design_consequence: Use two turns. Generate global boxes first; decode one person per box. Keep short pose tokens as the strict-generative component and replace contour64 with UFO-style mask embedding retrieval. Evaluate only with predicted boxes; retain GT-box results as diagnosis.
